title: Board random audit of continuing education and the 7-day response
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A the Board shall conduct audits of randomly selected renewed licenses. It initiates an audit by sending the selected licensees a request to provide documentation that evidences completion of the required contact hours, and the name and date of licensees included in an audit shall be posted on the Board's website. Licensees who are not in compliance with the contact hour requirements, or who fail to provide the requested documentation within 7 days of receiving a request, shall be fined not more than $1,000.
exam_relevance: Tests the statutory audit terms behind 247 CMR 4.06(2): the 7-day response period runs from receipt of the Board's request, and the fine of not more than $1,000 reaches both a late or missing production and a shortfall in contact hours.

numeric_facts.fact: time to provide requested continuing education documentation
numeric_facts.conditions: from receiving the Board's audit request

numeric_facts.fact: maximum fine for continuing education audit non-compliance
numeric_facts.conditions: contact hours not in compliance, or requested documentation not provided within 7 days

common_confusions: The 7 days run from the licensee's receipt of the Board's request, not from renewal.
The fine reaches two different failures: a shortfall in contact hours and a failure to provide the requested documentation in time.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24A on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
